summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on cipher-box PR #296, including automated reviewer (CodeRabbit/Copilot) nitpicks and human reviewer threads, by implementing fixes, committing, and formally replying to and resolving each thread.
summary.outcome: All 8 review threads resolved across two sessions: 6 from the initial /resolve-pr-reviews run and 2 more from a follow-up with additional nitpick comments. 7 code fixes were implemented and pushed; 1 comment was marked not applicable.

repo: cipher-box is a monorepo with packages: crypto, sdk, and an apps/web React frontend, plus tests/e2e with Playwright
The SDK uses lifecycle hook callbacks (config callbacks) that can throw and break operations — a notifySafely() wrapper pattern was introduced
Crypto key material (fileKey, folderKey) must be explicitly cleared with clearBytes() in finally blocks — the codebase treats key leakage as a security concern, not just a memory issue
Background re-wrap operations in createFolder share the folderKey buffer with the caller, requiring a defensive copy before passing to async work
ensureFolderRegistered in sdk-provider.ts can be called with unloaded placeholder folders that have empty keys — requires an isLoaded guard
ipns.service.ts had a stale doc comment referencing @cipherbox/crypto instead of @cipherbox/core that was already fixed in a prior commit before this session

code.finding: Post-upload path after fileKey generation was not wrapped in try/finally — fileKey could leak if an exception occurred before the re-wrap block's own cleanup
Lifecycle hook callbacks called without error isolation — a throwing hook could abort the entire operation; fixed with notifySafely() wrapper
createFolder passes folderKey buffer reference to background re-wrap — concurrent mutations risk; fixed with defensive copy + clearBytes in finally
ensureFolderRegistered lacked a guard for unloaded/placeholder folders with empty keys, risking registration with zero-length key material

Blob construction used .buffer on Uint8Array unnecessarily; direct Uint8Array works but TypeScript strict mode requires 'as BlobPart' cast due to Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> vs BlobPart incompatibility
180s timeout was too tight for 3 sequential wallet logins; increased to 300s
Context leak on failure during account creation — both createWalletTestAccount and createWalletTestAccounts needed cleanup in error paths

workflow: GitHub GraphQL API is required for fetching reviewThread isResolved status and for resolving threads (mutation); REST API is used for posting replies
Reply to PR threads uses gh api with --field for integer in_reply_to and --raw-field for string body
pnpm test / pnpm typecheck are the standard check commands; SDK-specific tests can be run in isolation
TypeScript strict mode can reject Uint8Array as BlobPart even though it works at runtime — requires explicit cast

friction: Unit tests were run as background tasks and results were not immediately available, requiring TaskOutput polling and a retry run to confirm passage
A stale lock file had to be removed before committing
The nitpick review (ID 3983247433) comments were outside-diff review-level comments, not thread comments, making them harder to fetch and reply to individually via the standard thread resolution flow
TypeScript rejected direct Uint8Array in Blob constructor due to strict generic typing (Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>), requiring an 'as BlobPart' workaround
open_items: Thread 2 from first session (concurrent mutations to same folder losing updates) was marked not applicable — acknowledged as an architectural concern for a follow-up PR, not this extraction PR
The notifySafely() lifecycle hook wrapper was added reactively; a broader audit of all config callback call sites for similar issues may be warranted
